newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC profits up in first 2 mths of 1997.
newsitem.headline: SBC profits up in first 2 mths of 1997.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) said its combined net profit for the months of January and February had already exceeded the profit realised for all of the 1996 first quarter.
Chief executive officer Marcel Ospel also said that in view of the persistent weakness of the Swiss economy, credit risk costs would be slightly higher in 1997.
In addition, he said in the text of a speech to banking sector analysts that the group had set an overall profit target to be reached by the year 1999 or 2000 of some 2.5 billion Swiss francs.

"The current year has got off to an excellent start for us, and we are very pleased with the results achieved so far: the accumulated net profit for January and February was well ahead of the results for the entire first quarter of 1996," Ospel said.
But he also said that in view of the continuing favourable financial market environment, it would be imprudent to extrapolate the results of two months to a full year.
"In view of the ongoing weakness in the Swiss economy we anticipate that expected credit risk costs (ACRA) will be slightly higher," Ospel also said.

"For the SBC group as a whole they (profit targets for each division) combine to make an overall profit target of some 2.5 billion Swiss francs by 1999/2000 on an estimated average equity base of around 16 billion Swiss francs. This corresponds to an after-tax return on equity of around 15 percent," Ospel also said.

He also said he expected the private banking unit to remain the group's strongest profit driver. But the group was looking for only moderate growth in profitability at SBC Warburg owing to the highly competitive environment and the resulting inevitable pressure on prices.
He said SBC had high expectations for a turnaround for SBC Switzerland and for accelerated profit growth at SBC Brinson in the U.S.
